etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English substituten, from Latin substitutus, past participle of substituō.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To use in place of something else, with the same function.
(transitive, in the phrase "substitute X for Y") To use X in place of Y.
(transitive, formerly proscribed, in the phrase "substitute X with/by Y") To use Y in place of X; to replace X with Y.
(transitive, sports) To remove (a player) from the field of play and bring on another in his place.

quote.citation: 2011 April 11, Phil McNulty, “Liverpool 3 - 0 Man City”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Mario Balotelli replaced Tevez but his contribution was so negligible that he suffered the indignity of being substituted himself as time ran out, a development that encapsulated a wretched 90 minutes for City and boss Roberto Mancini.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To serve as a replacement (for someone or something).

quote.citation: 1987, James Tobin, Essays in Economics, Vol. 2, page 75:
quote.text: Accumulation of wealth by this route may substitute for personal saving.

definitions.definition: A replacement or stand-in for something that achieves a similar result or purpose.

quote.citation: 1840 February, Thomas De Quincey, “Theory of Greek Tragedy”, in Leaders in Literature with a Notice of Traditional Errors Affecting Them (De Quincey’s Works; IX), London: James Hogg & Sons, →OCLC, footnote *, page 55:
quote.text: Ladies [in William Shakespeare's age], again, universally wore masks as the sole substitute known to our ancestors for the modern parasol; a fact, perhaps, not generally known.

quote.citation: 1965, “The Tracks of My Tears”, in Going to a Go-Go, performed by Smokey Robinson and The Miracles:
quote.text: Since you left me, if you see me with another girl / Seeming like I'm having fun / Although she may be cute, she's just a substitute / Because you're the permanent one

quote.citation: 1997, Quentin Tarantino, Jackie Brown, spoken by Ordell Robbie (Samuel L. Jackson):
quote.text: Here we go. AK-47. The very best there is. When you absolutely, positively got to kill every motherfucker in the room, accept no substitutes.

definitions.definition: (sports) A player who is available to replace another if the need arises, and who may or may not actually do so.

quote.citation: 2011 November 3, David Ornstein, “Macc Tel-Aviv 1 - 2 Stoke”, in BBC Sport‎[2]:
quote.text: Dean Whitehead opened the scoring shortly after the break with a low finish and substitute Peter Crouch sealed the win with a tap-in.

definitions.definition: (historical) One who enlists for military service in the place of a conscript.
